title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lynn, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lynn, CO | Raton Basin Coal Seam Gas
metaDescription: Own minerals near Lynn, CO in the Raton Basin? We check Vermejo/Raton coal seam gas well history before quoting, grounded in actual COGCC data.
heroLead: Lynn is a quiet corner of Las Animas County sitting over the same Raton Basin coal seams that have produced methane gas south of Trinidad for decades.
intro: Mineral ownership around Lynn typically traces back to ranch and grazing land that's remained in family hands for generations, with rights severed from surface use as the coalbed methane industry moved into the area starting in the 1990s. If you're holding a fractional interest here, it's most likely from that era of leasing activity rather than anything more recent.

sections.heading: What to expect from a CBM well near Lynn
paragraphs: Coal seam gas wells in this part of the Raton Basin ramp up slowly as water is produced off the coal to release gas, then settle into a long, gradually declining tail. A well with two decades of history behind it gives us real data to value against, which is often more reliable than the early-stage projections used for newer shale plays.
We check the specific well or wells tied to your legal description through Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission records, since production varies well to well even within the same coal seam.

sections.heading: Getting your ownership records in order
paragraphs: The Las Animas County clerk and recorder's office in Trinidad holds deed and lease history for this area. If your interest passed through multiple generations without formal probate, that can slow a sale, and we'll flag it early so you know what to expect before we get to closing.

faqs.question: How old are most of the wells around Lynn?
faqs.answer: Many date to the initial Raton Basin coalbed methane boom of the 1990s, with some later recompletion activity. We check each well's specific record rather than assuming a single age.

faqs.question: Does coal seam gas pay less than shale gas?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — it depends on the well's decline stage and current gas prices, not the resource type itself. We value against actual paid history, not assumptions about the play.

faqs.question: What if I only have a partial fractional interest?
faqs.answer: Common in this area given generations of inheritance. We quote fractional interests scaled to your documented share.

faqs.question: How do I confirm which well my Lynn interest is tied to?
faqs.answer: Send us your legal description and, if you have one, a division order statement. We match those against COGCC well records for the section before we quote anything.
